teams.heading: Fijian rugby player Saimoni Vunilagi dies of suspected heatstroke in Japan
teams.body: Fijian back-row forward Saimoni Vunilagi has died aged 26 after suffering suspected heatstroke following a training session in Japan. Vunilagi, who played for second-division side Kyushu KV, was hospitalised in Fukuoka after practice in early August, when temperatures reached 35 degrees Celsius. The 196cm forward passed away on Friday morning. Kyushu KV released a statement, saying that everyone was "devastated by this sudden news" over the loss of a player who only began his professional career in 2023.

lead.why: The tragic passing of Fijian rugby player Saimoni Vunilagi in Japan is the day's major and most widely covered story.

teams.heading: Ollie Lawrence and Elliot Daly lose England contracts in Borthwick revamp
teams.body: Steve Borthwick has overhauled his centrally contracted England squad for the 2026-27 season, making five changes to the 25-man list. Midfielders Ollie Lawrence and Elliot Daly are the headline omissions as Borthwick looks ahead to next year's World Cup, while winger Tom Roebuck and the injured Ben Curry also lose their £150,000 enhanced deals. In their place, prop Asher Opoku-Fordjour, lock Alex Coles, flanker Guy Pepper, scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet and centre Seb Atkinson all secure elite contracts for the first time.

lead.why: The omission of established stars Ollie Lawrence and Elliot Daly from England's new central contract list is a major selection shock ahead of the World Cup.

teams.heading: Former France kicking coach Vlok Cilliers joins Bulls after shock departure
teams.body: Former France kicking coach Vlok Cilliers has returned to South Africa, joining the Bulls' backroom staff following his surprise departure from Fabien Galthié's national setup. The French Rugby Federation recently confirmed the exit of Cilliers, who spent seven years honing Les Bleus' tactical kicking and Thomas Ramos's goal-kicking accuracy. Galthié sought a coaching shake-up, with defence specialist Shaun Edwards also reportedly relieved of his duties in May. France, who last beat Japan 42-15, must now restructure their backroom team ahead of their next fixture against Fiji.

teams.heading: Former Ireland half-back Brian Smith has died of cancer aged 59
teams.body: Tributes have poured in for former Ireland half-back Brian Smith, who has died of cancer at the age of 59. The Australian-born playmaker represented the Wallabies six times — including at the inaugural 1987 Rugby World Cup — before studying at Oxford University and earning nine caps for Ireland. Smith later transitioned to coaching, serving as England’s assistant coach between 2008 and 2011 and as director of rugby at London Irish. Wallabies prop Angus Bell, coached by Smith at Scots College, paid tribute to his former mentor.

lead.why: The rugby world is mourning the passing of former Ireland and Wallabies international playmaker Brian Smith.

teams.heading: Italy struggle defensively after conceding 318 points across 11 games
teams.body: Italy have struggled for consistency over their last 11 matches, scoring 190 points in total. At the other end, they conceded 318 points during that same period. Across those 11 games, Italy averaged 17.3 points scored and 28.9 points conceded per match. The high point of this 11-match window was a 34-19 home victory against Chile in November 2025 during the International Friendlies.

teams.heading: Scottish Rugby lawsuit pauses as judge considers striking out concussion claims
teams.body: The landmark brain injury litigation involving Scottish Rugby and other governing bodies has seen no fresh updates in today's press. Yesterday, reports highlighted that the legal battle had reached a critical juncture, with the presiding judge retiring to consider applications that could strike out up to 95% of the players' claims. The case remains at a standstill while the court deliberates these potential strikeouts, leaving both the claimants and the unions waiting on a pivotal ruling.

teams.heading: Former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones set for Ospreys board return
teams.body: Former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones is poised to return to the Ospreys as a board director next week. The 40-year-old’s expected appointment comes at a highly turbulent time for Welsh rugby, with the Ospreys fighting for survival under controversial Welsh Rugby Union plans to cut the country's professional sides from four to three. While Cardiff and the Dragons are expected to receive licences, the Ospreys face a straight battle against the Scarlets for the sole remaining regional spot in the west.

lead.why: Alun Wyn Jones is poised to make a highly anticipated return to the Ospreys as a board director next week.

teams.heading: Argentina playmaker Tomás Albornoz suspended for four matches after referee incident
teams.body: Argentina playmaker Tomás Albornoz has been handed a four-match suspension after accepting a misconduct charge for intimidating referee Angus Gardner. The incident occurred following the Pumas' dramatic 31-24 defeat against England, where a disallowed late try denied Argentina a chance to level the match. Albornoz approached the Australian official twice and had to be restrained by teammates. The ban rules the fly-half out of the recent clash with South Africa, the upcoming double-header against Australia, and a domestic fixture with Toulon.

lead.why: This disciplinary ruling directly impacts Argentina's squad selection and addresses the fallout from their last-reported match against England.

teams.heading: Taniela Tupou doubles up as Wallabies crush Japan 56-17 in Townsville
teams.body: Australia secured their first home Test victory under head coach Les Kiss, routing Japan 56-17 in Townsville on Saturday. The Wallabies ran in eight tries — including a double from prop Taniela Tupou and a debut score for Massimo De Lutiis — to seal three consecutive wins. After leading 21-17 at half-time, Australia unleashed 35 unanswered second-half points. Japan coach Eddie Jones conceded his side spent 'a long time on the defensive' as the hosts dominated the breakdown.

lead.why: The dominant 56-17 victory over Japan secures Les Kiss's first home win and a third consecutive Test victory.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones laments possession deficit as Australia overpower Japan in Townsville
teams.body: The Brave Blossoms suffered a fourth consecutive Test defeat on Saturday, falling 56-17 to Australia in Townsville. Despite a competitive first half featuring tries from Harry Hockings, Naoto Saito and Dylan Riley, Japan collapsed after the interval to concede 35 unanswered points. Eddie Jones highlighted a lack of possession and "aerial battles" as primary failings, noting: "In order for us to compete properly against such an opponent, we need to maintain more than 50 per cent possession." The result leaves Japan searching for tactical answers before the autumn.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie recalls Richie Mo'unga but rules out an immediate Test return
teams.body: Head coach Dave Rennie has added Richie Mo'unga to the All Blacks squad as an injury replacement for Billy Proctor. The 56-Test fly-half, who recently returned from Japan, is "jumping out of his skin" according to Rennie but will not feature in Saturday's series opener against the Springboks. Mo'unga is instead earmarked for a potential appearance against the Lions during the tour. The call-up follows a clinical 50-19 victory over the Bulls, which saw hooker Codie Taylor successfully return from injury to captain the side.

lead.why: The return of Richie Mo'unga to the national squad as an injury replacement is the day's biggest selection story.

teams.heading: Bulls open negotiations to bring Springboks star Malcolm Marx back home
teams.body: The Bulls have reportedly opened talks to lure Springboks hooker Malcolm Marx back to South Africa from Japan’s Kubota Spears. According to *Rapport*, the Pretoria outfit has identified the reigning World Rugby Player of the Year to bolster a front row facing several impending departures. While Rassie Erasmus prepares for the upcoming All Blacks series, the Bulls also face losing backline stars Embrose Papier and Canan Moodie to overseas interest. Erasmus noted the squad is "ready to give everything" following their recent 17-10 victory over Argentina.

lead.why: The potential return of the reigning World Rugby Player of the Year to South African domestic rugby is a major talking point for fans.
